title: Horizon Simulation
description: A black hole is the densest possible computer. Feed it a star and it will simulate one. Unlocks the Eye of the Event Horizon.

puzzle.goal: A black hole is grown from nothing by adding mass m slowly; each addition dE = c² dm is absorbed at the hole's thermal temperature ħc³/(8πG kB m), so its entropy rises by dE/T. Integrate up to the final mass M and convert the entropy into a number of bits.
puzzle.name: Black-hole information capacity (Bekenstein–Hawking from the first law)
puzzle.ask: The integral gives S = 4πG kB M²/(ħc) = π kB rs²/l², with rs = 2GM/c² and l the Planck length. Find the number of bits for a horizon radius of r = @{r} Planck lengths.
puzzle.method: Use dS = dE/T with the temperature of a hole of mass m, integrate from 0 to M, and divide by kB ln 2 per bit.
